pod_concurrency.decision: This frozen fifteen-case App Pod screen compared two, three and four workers with Pod requests, memory limits, outer executor sizing and case ownership fixed. The four-worker default is now on devel; these are historical measurements at the linked benchmark source.
pod_concurrency.scope: Two uncached actions per setting, ordered 2/3/4 then 4/3/2. All 90 JUnit case executions passed. Identical input trees and executor properties; Commands differ only by the case-limit environment variable. Infrastructure was warm, fixtures were distinct, and cleanup completed. This is an action screen, not complete PR feedback or a fleet failure-rate estimate. Control setup averaged 17 seconds slower than four-worker setup, so the full 21.4% action difference cannot all be attributed to concurrency; the case envelope fell 23.6%.
pod_concurrency.memory_finding: No memory setting changed. Maximum whole-action memory was 4.95 GiB at two workers, 4.99 at three and 4.87 at four. Kubelet samples retained at least about 4.70 GiB available and sampled up to five concurrent runtime Pods in the four-worker arm. Before-import/final snapshots contain no FailedScheduling, OOMKilled or eviction reasons. Ten-second sampling and final snapshots can miss transient events.
limitations: No cold-start, p90 or fleet reliability claim
Internal executor retries are not fully observable from indexed execution/JUnit records
Snapshot and ten-second sampling evidence is not exhaustive
followups: Full devel validation and independent port completed in merged PR #16659; the 22-case cohort is recorded separately.

devel_pod_concurrency.decision: Four Pod case slots landed through PR #16659. In its frozen unsplit 22-case cohort, all cases passed and mean action time fell from 363.3s to 289.2s (20.4%); the case envelope fell 29.8%. Pod requests, memory limits and executor sizing stayed fixed. The current required inventory is partitioned differently, so this is not a new port measurement.
devel_pod_concurrency.scope: Two fresh actions per setting, sequential order 2/4/4/2, with all 88 JUnit case executions passing. Input trees, executor properties and case identities are identical; decoded Commands differ only in the case-limit environment variable. All fixtures were distinct, infrastructure was warm, and cleanup completed. Mean setup was 35.2s at two slots and 40.4s at four; setup variation is separate from case concurrency. This small action screen does not establish whole-PR savings, p90, cold-start behavior or a fleet reliability rate. Two-slot action times ranged 335.6–391.1s; four-slot times ranged 285.2–293.1s. One trust probe took 94.5s in the slower control versus 12–17s elsewhere; its wait is not subdivided in existing traces, so that outlier is not attributed to concurrency. Against the faster control alone, the four-slot mean is 13.8% shorter; this is a sensitivity comparison, not a confidence bound.
devel_pod_concurrency.memory_finding: Maximum whole-action memory was 5.07 GiB at two slots and 5.12 GiB at four. Kubelet samples retained at least 4.51 GiB available and sampled up to 5 runtime Pods in the four-slot arm. Before-import/final snapshots contain no FailedScheduling, OOMKilled or eviction reasons. Ten-second sampling and snapshots can miss transient events.
